title: "Rows and columns"

Methods that read, select, filter, sort, and add rows and columns.

## Size and names

### `->columns()` {#columns}

```php
$table->columns(): array
```

Column names in order.

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `list<string>`\
**Examples** [Expressions](../expr.qmd)

### `->types()` {#types}

```php
$table->types(): array
```

Column types by name.

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `array<string, Type>`

### `->type()` {#type}

```php
$table->type(string $name): Type
```

One column's type.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$name` | <code>string</code> |  |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `Type`\
**Throws** `ColumnNotFound`: when the column does not exist.

### `->nrow()` {#nrow}

```php
$table->nrow(): int
```

Number of rows. SqlTable runs a COUNT(*) query.

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `int`\
**Examples** [Types](../types.qmd)

### `->ncol()` {#ncol}

```php
$table->ncol(): int
```

Number of columns.

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `int`

### `->count()` {#count}

```php
$table->count(): int
```

Number of rows, for count(`$df`).

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `int`

### `->has()` {#has}

```php
$table->has(string $name): bool
```

Whether the column exists.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$name` | <code>string</code> |  |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `bool`

## Selecting and renaming

### `->select()` {#select}

```php
$table->select(array $names): Table
```

Keep the named columns, in the given order.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$names` | <code>list&lt;string&gt;</code> |  | Column names. |

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `Table`\
**Throws** `ColumnNotFound`: when a column does not exist.\
**Examples** [Expressions](../expr.qmd), [Getting started](../getting-started.qmd), [phibble for Laravel developers](../laravel.qmd)

### `->rename()` {#rename}

```php
$table->rename(array $map): Table
```

Rename columns.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$map` | <code>array&lt;string, string&gt;</code> |  | New name => old name, as in dplyr. |

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `Table`\
**Throws** `ColumnNotFound`: when an old name does not exist.\
**Examples** [Getting started](../getting-started.qmd)

### `NameRepair::repair()` {#namerepair-repair}

```php
NameRepair::repair(
    array $names,
    Closure|string $mode = 'check_unique',
): array
```

Repair column names, as `vctrs::vec_as_names()`.

Modes: minimal makes names non-null; unique adds a ...n suffix to empty, `...`, `..j`, and duplicated names; check_unique throws unless names are unique and non-empty; universal is unique and also makes names syntactic in R. A closure receives the names and returns the repaired list.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$names` | <code>list&lt;string&#124;null&gt;</code> |  |  |
| `$mode` | <code>string&#124;Closure(list&lt;string&gt;): list&lt;string&gt;</code> | <code>'check_unique'</code> | minimal, unique, check_unique, universal, or a closure. |

**Static method** of `Phibble\NameRepair`\
**Returns** `list<string>`\
**Throws** `InvalidArgumentException`: when check_unique finds empty or duplicated names, or a closure returns a different number of names.

## Filtering and sorting

### `->filter()` {#filter}

```php
$table->filter(Closure|Expr $predicate): Table
```

Keep rows where the predicate is true. NA counts as false.

A closure runs once per row. An Expr runs once per group, a whole column at a time, so aggregates such as `mean()` compare within the group.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$predicate` | <code>Closure(Row, Table): ?bool&#124;Expr</code> |  | A row closure or an expression. |

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `Table`\
**Examples** [Reading and writing data](../io.qmd), [Expressions](../expr.qmd), [Getting started](../getting-started.qmd)

### `->arrange()` {#arrange}

```php
$table->arrange(array $keys): Table
```

Sort rows. The sort is stable, and NA sorts last in both directions.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$keys` | <code>list&lt;string&#124;array{0: string, 1?: 'asc'&#124;'desc'}&#124;Expr&gt;</code> |  | A column name sorts ascending; [name, 'desc'] sorts descending; an Expr sorts by its value, and `desc()` reverses it. |

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `Table`\
**Examples** [Getting started](../getting-started.qmd), [Types](../types.qmd), [phibble for Laravel developers](../laravel.qmd)

### `->distinct()` {#distinct}

```php
$table->distinct(array $names = []): Table
```

Unique rows over the named columns, keeping the first of each and only those columns.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$names` | <code>list&lt;string&gt;</code> | <code>[]</code> | Columns to compare. An empty list compares all columns. |

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `Table`\
**Examples** [Getting started](../getting-started.qmd)

### `->dropNa()` {#dropna}

```php
$table->dropNa(array $names = []): DataFrame
```

Drop rows with NA in any of the named columns (all columns when empty).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$names` | <code>list&lt;string&gt;</code> | <code>[]</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `DataFrame`\
**Examples** [Getting started](../getting-started.qmd)

## Adding columns and rows

### `->mutate()` {#mutate}

```php
$table->mutate(array $columns): Table
```

Add or replace columns.

Each value is a closure run per row, an Expr evaluated per group (aggregates repeat within the group), a list with one value per row, or a scalar to repeat. Later entries can use earlier ones.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$columns` | <code>array&lt;string, Closure(Row, Table): mixed&#124;list&lt;mixed&gt;&gt;</code> |  | New column name => value. |

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `Table`\
**Examples** [Expressions](../expr.qmd), [Getting started](../getting-started.qmd), [Types](../types.qmd)

### `->withColumn()` {#withcolumn}

```php
$table->withColumn(
    string $name,
    Column\Column|array $values,
    Type|string|null $type = null,
): DataFrame
```

Add or replace one column. Replaced columns keep their position.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$name` | <code>string</code> |  |  |
| `$values` | <code>list&lt;mixed&gt;&#124;Column</code> |  |  |
| `$type` | <code>Type&#124;string&#124;null</code> | <code>null</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `DataFrame`

### `->addColumn()` {#addcolumn}

```php
$table->addColumn(
    array $columns,
    string|int|null $before = null,
    string|int|null $after = null,
): DataFrame
```

Insert columns, as tibble's `add_column()`, with `tibble()`'s recycling rules. Place them before or after a column, by name or 0-based position; by default at the end.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$columns` | <code>array&lt;string, mixed&gt;</code> |  |  |
| `$before` | <code>string&#124;int&#124;null</code> | <code>null</code> |  |
| `$after` | <code>string&#124;int&#124;null</code> | <code>null</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `DataFrame`

### `->addRow()` {#addrow}

```php
$table->addRow(
    array $rows = [],
    ?int $before = null,
    ?int $after = null,
): DataFrame
```

Insert rows, as tibble's `add_row()`. Pass one row (name => value), a list of rows, or nothing for an all-NA row. Missing columns are NA; unknown columns throw. Positions are 0-based: `$before` inserts before that row, `$after` after it. The default appends.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$rows` | <code>array&lt;string, mixed&gt;&#124;list&lt;array&lt;string, mixed&gt;&gt;</code> | <code>[]</code> |  |
| `$before` | <code>?int</code> | <code>null</code> |  |
| `$after` | <code>?int</code> | <code>null</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `DataFrame`

## Rows by position

### `->slice()` {#slice}

```php
$table->slice(int $offset, ?int $length = null): Table
```

Rows from `$offset`, `$length` of them or to the end. Ignores groups.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$offset` | <code>int</code> |  | 0-based start; negative counts from the end. |
| `$length` | <code>int&#124;null</code> | <code>null</code> | Number of rows; null for the rest, negative to stop that many rows before the end. |

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `Table`

### `->head()` {#head}

```php
$table->head(int $n = 6): Table
```

The first `$n` rows. Ignores groups.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$n` | <code>int</code> | <code>6</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `Table`\
**Examples** [Getting started](../getting-started.qmd), [phibble for Laravel developers](../laravel.qmd), [Types](../types.qmd)

### `->tail()` {#tail}

```php
$table->tail(int $n = 6): DataFrame
```

The last n rows; a negative n drops the first \|n\| rows, as in R.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$n` | <code>int</code> | <code>6</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `DataFrame`

### `->take()` {#take}

```php
$table->take(array $indices): Table
```

Rows by 0-based position, in the given order. A null index gives an all-NA row.

Types, factor levels, and grouping are kept.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$indices` | <code>list&lt;int&#124;null&gt;</code> |  |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`, `SqlTable`, `PolarsTable`\
**Returns** `Table`
